title: NACD Chicago's CEO picks Eric as one of the Summit's three most provocative talks — 'Could conventional governance practices actually undermine the great companies directors are supposed to protect?'
summary: Hedges runs the Chicago chapter of the National Association of Corporate Directors and brought more than 170 of its members to the Summit. Writing up the mainstage, he singles out three presentations worth reflecting on and puts Eric alongside Ian Bremmer on geopolitical risk and Jesse Cohn of Elliott Investment Management on activist investors. His framing of the talk is a question aimed at his own membership: whether the governance practices directors are trained in are the thing putting good companies at risk. He adds that he did not agree with everything he heard, which is what made the conversations worthwhile.
blockquote: Could conventional governance practices actually undermine the great companies directors are supposed to protect?
